correctness.rationale: For compact convex 0∈K⊂RB and continuous nonnegative nondecreasing radial φ with C2 away from 0 and nonnegative radial Laplacian, the smooth outer parallel derivative is ∫_{∂(K+sB)}H_s φ + ∫_{K+sB}Δφ. Positivity bounds the flux integral by the radius-(R+s) ball; bounding φ by φ(R+s) and total mean curvature through inclusion-monotone W2 gives derivative <=G′(R+s) with G(R)=nω_nR^(n−1)φ(R). Keeping the discarded Δ term gives the stated deficit. Origin-containing inclusion monotonicity and multiplicity-corrected perimeter continuity, explicitly cited primary antecedents, provide the lower bound and pass to degenerate K. Minkowski interpolation h_u=(1−u)h_K+u h_L has Hausdorff speed d_H(K,L); subdivision and the parallel estimate yield sharp Lipschitz coefficient G′(R). Concentric ball radii R and R−ε attain the limiting ratio. Power φ=r^p (p>0) obeys the flux and Δ assumptions even 0<p<1. Independent exact/numerical integrations checked 4 rectangles and parallel arcs against the ball envelope, not a proof for all convex bodies. A positive Δ almost everywhere yields strict deficit for proper K. The common center and subharmonicity assumptions are essential.
